discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and Cirac showed theoretically that cold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models with tunable parameters. They also proposed controlled interactions as a route to quantum gates and entanglement. Bloch's landmark observation of the superfluid–Mott insulator transition (2002) turned this proposal into reality. His later quantum-gas microscopy, many-body localization studies and Fermi-Hubbard experiments established the field. Together these achievements founded analog quantum simulation, Feynman's idea of using one controllable quantum system to solve problems that classical computers cannot. The approach turned atomic physics into a laboratory for condensed-matter questions such as quantum magnetism, topological bands and non-equilibrium dynamics. It created a platform that is now adopted worldwide. The same concepts underpin today's programmable neutral-atom quantum processors and error-corrected logical qubits. This combination of conceptual insight and transformative experiment links fundamental many-body physics with quantum information science.
